industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 (Jefferies, 22 Oct), oil above $100 and rising, and energy led the week; energy is the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior at industry level. Not Double Overweight at the industry because the industry holds Metals and mining (relative strength F now from A) and Agriculture beside the three energy sectors; Downstream distribution carries the A. Counter-case: Goldman attributes part of the oil move to restocking, two months into leadership is where reversals begin, and 13 of the 18 upstream Pool names read F on TSR/Valuation, so the market has paid.

sector.why: Overweight, carried. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Brent near $115 and oil the inflation risk Goldman Sachs worries about most, with Iran the two-sided swing; Equinor solid with a lifted production guide and a balance sheet that pressures it to raise buybacks (Danske Bank, 28 October); against it, Nordic exploration and production names lagged as crude eased on de-escalation (DNB Carnegie, 26 October) and Rosebank was written into the UK's fiscal arithmetic. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: A now, A prior, agrees. Eighteen Pool names, the largest sector in the Pool, with 15 energy names in the top 40 of the starting score, which is why the sector cap on the Lists (component 5, amendment 6) stays. Counter-case: producers move with crude and crude eased late in the week. Back to C if Brent falls under $85.

geography.why: Neutral, carried as a judgement with the evidence now read both ways, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': the Budget removed a UK-specific fiscal tail risk from the discount rate without lowering it (headroom £15bn, both rules met, the 10-year gilt about 5.32% and its lowest in over a month, gilts outperforming Bunds and Treasuries by about 5 basis points), and the UK data beat on every count (growth 0.7% on three months, employment up 102,000, purchasing managers' indices beating; Pacific, 26 October); against it, 2027 growth cut to 1.0% from 1.6%, unemployment 5.1% in 2027, the energy price cap up about 16% in January, a Bank of England rise to 4.00% almost priced for 5-Nov-26, and banks made the first payer in the next shock. Neutral against Underweight was tested; the data say the consumer slows rather than breaks, so Neutral, with no weight carried in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). 22 of the 144 Pool stocks are UK-listed. Counter-case: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance on 5-Nov-26, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.
